label: TP
reason: User-supplied header value flows directly into the HTML response via concatenation without any encoding or filtering. The CodeQL report correctly identifies two paths: (1) the decoded header value assigned to param then passed to doSomething which returns it unchanged, and (2) the session attribute name derived from the same header also returned by doSomething. Both strings are printed to the HTTP response body, allowing script injection.

evidence.note: Response writer prints user variable containing unencoded header input
doSomething returns param unchanged enabling direct reflection
